bumpVersions.name: cargo-package-version: on a dependency upgrade, patch-bump this crate's own [package].version in Cargo.toml so the existing auto-tag.yml -> release.yml chain fires and the updated dependency lands in a release without a manual bump PR. lockFileMaintenance does not change a dependency version string, so it is not expected to trigger this. NOTE: matchStrings are compiled with re2, which rejects lookahead/lookbehind ('invalid perl operator: (?!') -- a regex using one fails to compile and the whole rule silently no-ops. Stay inside the [package] table with the negated class [^\[] (matches across newlines, stops at the next [section]) instead of a negative lookahead, and line-anchor with (?m)^\s*version so rust-version is not matched.

packageRules.description: Consumer-side workflows THIS layer renders (`ci.yml.tera`, `auto-tag.yml.tera`, both `when = "always"`). Action bumps happen upstream in pj-rust and flow down via `kata apply`, so a Renovate-driven local bump is reverted on the next apply and re-opened forever. The canonical pins live in `.kata/vars.toml`, which pj-base's customManager scans. Owned here rather than in pj-base because pj-base cannot know that a Rust layer composes above it.

The `editorconfig_checker` pin is kata-managed in consumer repos (back-filled into `.kata/vars.toml` via this layer's `merge-toml, when=always` entry, unlike the consumer-owned `swatinem_rust_cache` pin). The canonical bump happens in pj-rust's own `vars.rust.toml` and flows down on the next `kata apply` — a consumer-side Renovate bump would be reverted by that apply, re-opened by Renovate, and so on. Disable consumer-side scanning of this one dep to break the cycle.
